summary: This is episode 3 of a daily Ramadan Tafsir series focused on Surah Ar-Ra'd. The scholar provides detailed exegesis of the opening verses of the chapter, discussing the Quranic letters (Alif Lam Meem Ra), the meaning of "Kitab" (book), and how revelation came to the Prophet Muhammad through various means including true dreams, visions, and miracles. The lecture emphasizes that the Quran contains the essence of all previous scriptures revealed by Allah. A significant portion addresses why most people disbelieve despite receiving clear truth—explaining that disbelief stems from human desires and emotions rather than logical reasoning. The scholar also discusses the Arabs' pre-Islamic beliefs, clarifying that they acknowledged Allah as the sole Creator but committed shirk by worshiping saints as intermediaries, and explains the theological principle of accepting Quranic descriptions of Allah's attributes without questioning the "how" (kayf), as established by the Salaf.
